title: REC-04: staged renderer optimization milestones Aâ€“G (local GPU + CI evidence)
body:
## Objective
Migrate Beckenburg's renderer from per-frame CPU scene construction/lighting into prepared, retained GPU resources while preserving the existing Java 17/LibGDX renderer, authored assets, gameplay rules, and working release gates.

**Authoritative implementation spec:** [Rendering Milestones Aâ€“G](https://github.com/mrcalzon02/The-Beckenburg-Project/blob/main/development/performance/RENDERING_MILESTONES_A-G.md)

**Baseline SHA:** `5909f66a6314666fd5f5a6cf4e86847eb11a7314`
**First source checkpoint:** [`003b72e`](https://github.com/mrcalzon02/The-Beckenburg-Project/commit/003b72e4871d093e0fcfb9b3e6727029a0550d82)

### Milestone ledger
- [ ] **A. Measured performance baseline** â€” 33-frame same-renderer House GPU waypoint profile source is committed; accept only after successful same-SHA GPU CI and usable CSV/artifacts. Extend to collision-respecting player path and real hardware p50/p95/p99.
- [ ] **B. PreparedScene, SceneState and resident GPU geometry** â€” stable chunk/mesh identities, GL-thread lifecycle, world-space static buffers, truly separate dynamic instances. Prove camera rotation does not rebuild/upload static geometry.
- [ ] **C. Room/portal visibility** â€” conservative room/door/window/stair culling, outdoor cells; preserve visual correctness across all door states.
- [ ] **D. Independent static/dynamic lighting** â€” immutable geometry unaffected by switches, localized shadows/probes, exact ghost/evidence pulses and physical wall occlusion.
- [ ] **E. GPU composition** â€” profile synchronization and glReadPixels, then migrate sprites/effects/depth passes without breaking ghost concealment, fonts or CPU recovery.
- [ ] **F. Loading/warmup and site flyover** â€” explicit ready-to-render state after asset preparation; flight ends with responsive van control. Preserve diagnostic context for issue #6.
- [ ] **G. Multi-map installed acceptance** â€” House, Farmhouse, School, Castle and older maps; actual Windows GPU hardware, single-player and TCP round, presets, editor, memory and 30 FPS target on defined hardware.

### Local Codex workstation handoff
1. Checkout current main; inspect AGENTS.md, development/RECOVERY_PLAN_2026-10-25.md and the Aâ€“G specification.
2. Prepare the approved source assets using repository build instructions, then build the GPU client with `mvn -B -ntp -f gpu-client/pom.xml -DskipTests package`.
3. Run the GPU acceptance on the real Windows GPU using the packaged `BeckenburgGPU.jar --gpu-smoke` path (full command depends on the generated launcher/asset working directory). Preserve `build/e2e/gpu/continuous-route.csv`, the summary and captures.
4. Record GPU model, driver, JVM, viewport, presets, screen resolution, SHA, JVM/GC logs, per-frame readback and upload timings, and repeat runs before drawing p95 comparisons.
5. Commit small reversible batches; do not force-push or replace concurrent work. Confirm every remote SHA and same-SHA workflow. Do not suppress functional regressions or add unsolicited cosmetic release gates.

### Acceptance discipline
Do not merge phases blindly. Baselines should be compared on the same machine, driver, graphics settings and camera trace. Mesa llvmpipe tests correctness and variability, not dedicated-GPU performance. No claim that source commit or successful packaging alone proves that issue #6's installed case-start hang is resolved.
